newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Hutu refugees arrive at Angola's border with Congo.
newsitem.headline: Hutu refugees arrive at Angola's border with Congo.

text.p: About 1,400 Hutu refugees, fleeing uncertainty in Laurent Kabila's Democratic Republic of the Congo, have arrived at Angola's far eastern border post at Luau after a nine-month journey, aid officials said on Monday.
They quoted some refugees as saying Angolan guards had shot dead 25 others when they tried to enter at another crossing in May.
Relief workers who interviewed the group estimated they had walked over 1,500 kilometres (900 miles) in flight from Kabila's rebels who toppled Zaire's president Mobutu Sese Seko in May.
"The last estimate had the number of refugees at around 1,400," Madi Diallo, country director of Medecins sans Frontieres (Belgium) told Reuters.

"They appear to be all of Hutu descent, mostly from Rwanda but there are also some from Burundi," Diallo said, adding: "The health situation is not good and there are signs of malnutrition among the children."
The refugees told aid workers they tried to enter Angola at its northern border at Dundo in May, but Angolan government forces had fired at them, killing 25.
"They say that the Angolan police or soldiers killed around 25 of the people who were travelling with them," one relief worker said.

The group was also earlier prevented from entering the country further to the east by former rebel UNITA troops. Aid officials say the refugees said they were mostly from a refugee camp near Uvira in the east of the new Congo, while others were from Bukavu and Goma.
Thousands of Hutus poured across the border into the then Zaire from neighbouring Rwanda after a 1994 genocide that killed several hundred thousand of the country's minority Tutsis.

In October and November last year the camps were abandoned as the refugees fled either into nearby jungles or back to their homeland, fearing Kabila's rebels who were backed by Rwanda's new Tutsi-led government.
Aid workers and foreign media have alleged that Kabila's forces or their allies have massacred thousands of Hutus in the jungles of eastern Congo.
The U.N.'s refugee agency (UNHCR) refused to comment on the presence of the Hutus in Luau.
